events.text: At the House of Tea on the Ninth Isle the peach-sellers have gone quiet. Their stock tastes of nothing this year, and old Peiwen swears the Drifting Orchard has swung back into the lanes, trailing blossom, to be picked clean by whoever dares.

choices.text: Ask Peiwen how the orchard drifts

effects.log: She draws a loop in spilled tea: the old wind-road of a House long gone. You copy it onto your sleeve.

choices.text: Buy a flavourless peach anyway

effects.log: It tastes of nothing, and of a faint ache for something. You begin to understand why people go.

variants: The peach-sellers at the House of Tea on the Ninth Isle have nothing worth selling: their fruit tastes of nothing this year. Old Peiwen swears it means the Drifting Orchard is back in the lanes, trailing blossom, for whoever dares.

events.text: {sr_sect} sends its party in over the orchard's low bridge, a plank of cloud-wood that bears only those who walk in step. The leader counts the stride aloud. Everyone feels foolish and nobody misses a beat. Beyond the bridge the first trees already lean toward you.

choices.text: Keep step and count with them

effects.log: The bridge hums under a hundred feet and holds. You cross as part of something, which is rarer than it sounds.

choices.text: Break step to see what the bridge does

effects.log: It sags a hand-span and sighs, like a disappointed teacher. Nobody falls. Everyone remembers.

events.text: You skip the bridge and climb in by the windfall chute, where the orchard drops its spoiled fruit into the void. It is slick with rotten peach and smells of sweet vinegar. Somewhere above, the pickers' songs wobble out of tune.

choices.text: Climb quietly

effects.log: Your hands remember how, or learn it fast. You roll over the lip into a lane of petals with not a bruise.

choices.text: Eat a windfall for strength

effects.log: It is half rot and half sugar, and it hits your head like a gong. The next hour is brighter than it deserves to be.

events.text: The safe road is the pickers' lane, hung with paper tags in the colours of every House that rents a tree. Rival parties argue over whose tag hangs lowest. You pass six disputes before noon and are drawn into none, which is its own small skill.

choices.text: Settle one dispute for a quiet word

effects.log: A ruling on a mere branch, but both sides remember who gave it. The lane widens for you after that.

choices.text: Memorise who owns which tree

effects.log: Tags are ledgers, if you can read them. By dusk you know which Houses are rich in fruit and which in grudges.

events.text: The beast road runs through the ox-meadow, where the orchard's cloud-oxen graze on the low blossom. They are the size of barns and dislike strangers on their grass. One lifts its head, and the whole herd turns with it, slow as weather.

choices.text: Stand still and let them smell you

effects.log: Breath like warm rain passes over your face. They decide you are a very small tree and go back to grazing.

choices.text: Slip along the fence in a crouch

effects.log: You make it past four oxen. The fifth lets you reach the gap, then drops a cloud of pollen on you. Sneezing begins.

events.text: The hidden road begins at a peach tree whose knothole you carved a lifetime ago into a sulking face. In the hollow behind it is a jar of fruit paste sealed in your own hand, and a note: Do not share it with the ox.

choices.text: Eat the paste

effects.log: It is a century old and sweeter than grief. For an hour you remember being someone who knew all the paths here.

choices.text: Share it with the ox anyway

effects.log: The first one you meet takes it from your palm. After this it follows you for miles, humming through its nose.

events.text: The cloud-ox kneels in the grass, snorting blossom. It was never trying to hurt you, only to keep the last tree's roots from being trodden, and it knows it has met a better guardian than itself. It noses the fruit toward you, and for a heartbeat looks very old.

choices.text: Scratch it between the horns

effects.log: It leans into your hand with its whole weight. You are nearly toppled by gratitude.

choices.text: Take the peach and bow

effects.log: It drops from the bough into your hands, heavy as a lantern. The ox watches, calm. It has done its part.

events.text: The ox lifts you in its horns like a sack, carries you to the orchard's rim and sets you on a branch that bends but holds. It does not hurt you. It will simply not be passed, and it turns back to chew, perfectly satisfied that the matter is closed.

choices.text: Laugh, and climb down

effects.log: You have been bested by an animal with a mouthful of flowers. It is humbling, and rather clean.

choices.text: Count where it was weakest

effects.log: The left flank, where the old yoke-scar pulls. Next opening, you will be ready for it.

events.text: You stand in the meadow and hum the pickers' work song, the one with the slow ending. The ox listens with its whole head. Then it lowers it, and breathes warm blossom into your hands. It does not want to be ridden. It wants to be told it did well.

choices.text: Tell it so

effects.log: You say it quietly, and again. It closes its eyes. The peach, when it falls, falls straight into your palm.

choices.text: Ask what it guards

effects.log: It leads you to a lone sapling, a hand tall, which the orchard has been protecting for four centuries. You say nothing, and kneel.

events.text: {sr_sect} meets the party at the orchard's rim with a lacquered basket, and the peach goes in on a damp cloth under a seal. It will be sliced into a hundred portions by feast-day. The other baskets are weighed twice. One picker has bitten the stone-seed in hers, and thinks nobody saw.

choices.text: Tell the weighers about the seed

effects.log: It was a small theft and a small shame. The picker is fined a month of silence, and does not forgive you.

choices.text: Say nothing, and note who owes you

effects.log: A favour kept is worth a peach. You will not need to say it aloud.

events.text: Two rival pickers catch you at the last branch, polite as bailiffs, asking to share the peach. They counted your party and found it short. The orchard is leaving; the fruit rots at the speed of rumour. You have only a few breaths to decide what it is worth.

choices.text: Outrun them along the branch

ok.log: You swing from bough to bough, over their heads, and drop through the gate with the peach in your teeth.

fail.log: A bough gives. You land hard, and the peach is bruised and half theirs before the gate shuts.

choices.text: Split it and walk out as friends

effects.log: It is half what you hoped, and you keep your knees. They owe you a courtesy at the next fair.

events.text: On the Pilgrim Isle the lantern-makers wake to find every wick in the guild-hall lit by itself. Nobody trimmed them. Nobody has a spark to spare. The old riddle-teller says the Hall of Ten Thousand Lanterns is exhaling, and that one lantern in it has never been put out.

choices.text: Ask the riddle-teller which lantern

effects.log: She grins, shows you her hands, and says the answer is in the ones you did not carry. You write it down anyway.

choices.text: Help snuff the guild-hall wicks

effects.log: It takes all night. Your fingers smell of wax for a month. The wicks, relit, burn a little steadier for being asked.

variants: Every wick in the lantern-makers' guild-hall on the Pilgrim Isle was burning at dawn, and nobody lit one. The old riddle-teller nods: the Hall of Ten Thousand Lanterns is breathing out, and its one undying lamp is close.

The lanterns of the Pilgrim Isle light themselves at dusk this month, a street at a time, as if something were walking through the town with a taper. The Hall of Ten Thousand Lanterns is near, says the old riddle-teller.

events.text: {sr_sect} files into the Hall in pairs, each pair carrying a single lantern for the dark ahead, and the leader reminds everyone of the old rule: never let a lamp be lit from another's. A cough echoes among the hanging paper and a thousand flames bend toward the sound.

choices.text: Carry the lantern for your pair

effects.log: It is warm and surprisingly heavy. You find your breathing slows to match its flame.

choices.text: Whisper your lamp-name to it

effects.log: The flame brightens and hums back a half-tone. It is a courtesy, nothing more, and it feels like being known.

events.text: You enter between two lanterns that are not quite touching, where the paper wall has a seam. The air inside smells of hot oil and old prayers. Overhead, ten thousand lamps swing very slightly, like a crowd turning to look at one stranger and politely refusing to.

choices.text: Move only in the shadows between lamps

effects.log: You trace a dark lane through the glow. It is slow, careful work, and you finish it unseen.

choices.text: Cover your face with a sleeve

effects.log: It makes no sense and it works. The lamps lose interest in a face they cannot read.

events.text: The safe road follows the lamp-lit aisle, and every few steps a small lantern-spirit waits on its hook to take a coin of qi, a toll the Hall asks of all. Parties cluster at each hook, haggling with paper. You pay what the spirits ask and walk on, unhurried.

choices.text: Pay the toll in full

effects.log: The spirits glow and fold their wicks. The aisle ahead brightens a shade, an honest receipt.

choices.text: Haggle with the spirits

effects.log: They rustle, scandalised, and take half. You will not be allowed to forget it the whole way through.

events.text: The beast road passes the Moth Gallery, where lamp-moths the size of cart wheels circle the flames. They are not hostile, only drawn, and anything that glows draws them. You are carrying a lantern. A hush falls, and then the wings begin.

choices.text: Hide the lantern in your coat

effects.log: Darkness falls on your path. Moth-wings brush past, puzzled. You are grateful for every one that does not stay.

choices.text: Hold it high and walk calmly

effects.log: They surround you in a ring of soft dust and let you carry them along the gallery like a slow parade.

events.text: The hidden road runs through a door in the paper wall that only seems like part of a painted lantern. You open it with a word you thought you had forgotten. Beyond lies a corridor of single candles, each with a name, and one unlit at the end, already carrying yours.

choices.text: Light it yourself

effects.log: It catches without a spark. It will burn in the Hall for as long as you do, and you feel it as a warmth under the ribs.

choices.text: Leave it dark and walk on

effects.log: Unlit, it keeps your name safe. You feel strangely lighter, and strangely watched.

events.text: The lamplighter, a puppet of paper and brass, drops its long pole. Its painted face tilts toward you, and the hall's flames settle. It was built for one order: keep the lanterns lit. It sees now that you will keep them lit better than it could, and it folds, like a screen.

choices.text: Pick up the pole

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks. As you hold it the nearest flames lean toward you, trusting.

choices.text: Carry the lamplighter out in pieces

effects.log: It would rather stay and tend the hall. You take its painted face only, and leave the rest burning.

events.text: The lamplighter's pole catches your knees, your ribs, your guard, never hard, always exact. When you are down it snuffs the lamp you carried, calmly, as a servant removes a plate. The dark that follows is polite and total, and ends only when you crawl to the door.

choices.text: Crawl toward the nearest glow

effects.log: Hand by hand you find your way to a doorway and a light that was always going to be there.

choices.text: Sit in the dark and listen

effects.log: There is a tune in the hall, made of ten thousand wicks. You learn it by heart before you are let go.

events.text: You slip past the lamplighter by walking exactly as slowly as its swinging pole, one step in each shadow it throws. It is the strangest dance you have ever danced. It does not turn once, though it must know you are there. At the end it bows, a little.

choices.text: Bow back

effects.log: Whatever it is, it was made with manners. You leave on terms with a paper servant, and no shame in it.

choices.text: Count the steps for next time

effects.log: Eighty-one steps, nine shadows. A map you could walk in your sleep.

events.text: {sr_sect} hangs the Hall's flame in its own lantern-room at the party's return, behind glass, and sends for scribes to write down the exact shade. The party is thanked in order of the lamps it brought back lit. Yours is somewhere in the middle, and burns very bright.

choices.text: Ask where the flame will be kept

effects.log: The scribes consult one another, and tell you. It is more than most are told, and enough to find it again.

choices.text: Light your lamp from it

effects.log: A courtesy, they say; a theft, others whisper. The flame in your hand burns calm and blue.

events.text: At the Hall's door a cloaked lantern-thief waits with a hooded lamp of his own, asking to trade. He knows you carry the flame; he can tell by the way your shadow stands up. He is polite and he is not alone. A thousand little lights watch the exchange, ready to tell.

choices.text: Trade a half-measure of the flame

effects.log: He takes it with wonder, and lets you pass. By morning half the market has a thin blue wick.

choices.text: Snuff your lamp and slip away

effects.log: In the dark you are nobody. By the time he relights, you are a long way down the stair.

events.text: A crater-ringed isle that dropped from the sky a thousand years ago has begun to glow at its seams. The potters of the Ash Quarter say the Cold Kiln is warming. Somewhere under the slag, a firing order given at the fall is still waiting to be finished.

choices.text: Ask a potter what was fired

effects.log: Not pots, she says. Cauldrons, for immortals who died on the way up. She knocks twice on her own wall to be sure it is still hers.

choices.text: Gather slag from the crater edge

effects.log: It is warm in your hand and ringing. A whole season of quiet will not cool it.

variants: The crater isle that fell from the sky a thousand years ago glows along its seams again. In the Ash Quarter the potters say the Cold Kiln is waking, its last firing order still waiting under the slag.

events.text: {sr_sect} brings its own bellows-men, who set a fan of cold blue flame at the kiln mouth and walk the party in through it. The heat slides off like water on wax. The leader reminds you that it will not do so on the way out unless the party is whole.

choices.text: Stay close to the bellows-men

effects.log: They hum a low steady note as they walk. Your skin remembers the tune long after.

choices.text: Test the heat with a finger

effects.log: It bites. The bellows-man swats your hand, kindly, and says every year it is the same fool.

events.text: You find a flue that has rotted open and squeeze in through soot and slag-glass. The inside is warm like an animal. Once your eyes adjust you see runnels of cooled glaze on every wall, frozen mid-pour, like a river with a purpose.

choices.text: Crawl along the glaze

effects.log: It is smooth and does not give. You follow its slow downhill like a thread through a maze.

choices.text: Break off a bead of glaze

effects.log: It chimes. Somewhere deeper in the kiln a bell answers it, and you hurry to be elsewhere.

events.text: The safe road follows the old cart-rails through the cooling-yards, past rows of unfinished cauldrons laid out like sleeping cattle. Parties mark their routes with chalk. Some mark the same cauldron, and tempers rise. You walk through quarrels of fresh chalk, listening.

choices.text: Settle which party marked first

effects.log: Chalk dust and the dead cauldrons are witnesses enough. You split the aisle and leave nobody insulted.

choices.text: Study the unfinished cauldrons

effects.log: The mould-lines tell you the firing order, what was wanted and what was missed. You carry it away like a recipe.

events.text: The beast road goes down through the ash-pits, where slag-hounds nest. They are small, glowing, and look like dogs made of cinders. Hundreds lift their heads together as you pass, and the heat of their breath bends the air in rippling sheets.

choices.text: Toss them a scrap of dried meat

effects.log: They fall on it like a tide. One follows you for a mile, nose-glowing, wagging.

choices.text: Walk through without a sound

effects.log: Each hound turns its head as you pass, one after another, a glowing wave of attention. Not one barks.

events.text: The hidden road is a drain you once cleaned with your own hands, three lives ago. Brick by brick it comes back. At the bottom is an unfinished cauldron with your thumbprint in its clay and, curled inside, a small warm stone. It has been waiting patiently to be finished.

choices.text: Finish the cauldron with your thumb

effects.log: The clay takes your thumb as if it never left. The warmth in the stone goes quiet, at last, like a child put to bed.

choices.text: Pocket the warm stone

effects.log: It rests against your ribs, a tiny kiln. For days you are never cold.

events.text: The kiln-golem stops mid-swing, mouth glowing, and for the first time in a thousand years has nothing to fire. Its voice comes out as a long low roar. You understand it as: is the order done? Is it finished? Is it, at last, allowed to cool?

choices.text: Tell it the order is done

effects.log: The golem sets down its tongs. A long breath of heat leaves it, and the glow in its chest turns slowly from white to red.

choices.text: Take its tongs and its answer

effects.log: The tongs are warm, ringing like a bell. It does not argue. It cools with its eyes on you.

events.text: The golem pins you against a cold wall with its tongs and holds you there until the heat wears off your temper. It does not squeeze. It only waits, with the air of a very old workman who has seen apprentices of every kind and is not surprised by this one.

choices.text: Admit the firing is beyond you

effects.log: The tongs release at once. The golem hands you a bead of glaze, as a master gives a failing student one thing to keep.

choices.text: Struggle until it lets go

effects.log: It lets go when it feels like it. You will carry the bruise for a month and the lesson for longer.

events.text: You slip by the golem as it turns to stoke a vent, using the roar of the bellows to mask your steps. It is a trick as old as potters. When you look back it is staring at the place where you were, perplexed, tongs raised in an interrupted question.

choices.text: Leave a thank-you of chalk

effects.log: You scrawl a spiral on the nearest wall. The golem later copies it, endlessly. It is the nearest it has to a letter.

choices.text: Keep moving without looking back

effects.log: It does not follow. The kiln-light fades behind you to a patient glow.

events.text: {sr_sect} receives the party in the ash-courtyard, and the smiths take the cauldron-core in tongs lined with wet felt. It will be re-fired three times before anyone is allowed to look at it. They say it only needs finishing, which is what everyone says of everything unfinished.

choices.text: Ask to watch the first firing

effects.log: They refuse, and then relent. It takes a full night, and by dawn you can taste the metal in your breath.

choices.text: Offer to carry it yourself

effects.log: It is warm through the felt, heavy as a sleeping child. The smiths watch you closely, and say nothing.

events.text: Slag-runners from a rival workshop wait at the crater's lip, soot-faced and cheerful, with a barrow and the manners of undertakers. They would like the cauldron-core, as a favour to history. The kiln's glow dims behind you like a door closing. The ash is deep.

choices.text: Refuse politely and walk through them

effects.log: They are runners, not fighters. They part like smoke, and one mutters you have a good back for carrying.

choices.text: Drop a decoy glaze-bead in the barrow

effects.log: They fall over it in the ash, shouting. The real find is under your coat, warm and quiet.

events.text: The cloud-fishers of the Low Isles bring in empty nets for a month, and then one morning their floats all point the same way. The Cloud Reef is surfacing, they say: a bone-white shelf under the sea of mist, built by creatures that died upward. It comes up every twelve years to breathe.

choices.text: Ask a fisher to show you the floats

effects.log: They all point to one gap in the horizon. She taps it and says: that is where she sleeps. You do not ask who.

choices.text: Help mend the nets

effects.log: It is honest work, and by dusk you have the knots in your fingers and a story to match.

variants: A month of empty nets on the Low Isles, and then one morning every float points the same way. The fishers say the Cloud Reef is rising to breathe, as it does every twelve years: a bone-white shelf under the mist.

events.text: {sr_sect} hires a cloud-ferry with a hull of fine sky-silk, and the party poles out across the mist toward the reef's pale rim. The ferryman sings a warning song at the turn of every tide. The leader makes you promise not to drop anything overboard. Everything that falls is heard of again.

choices.text: Learn the ferryman's song

effects.log: It has twelve verses and each one is the name of something that took a boat. You commit them all to memory.

choices.text: Lean over the side to look

effects.log: Below the mist, pale shapes turn lazily. The ferryman pulls you back by the belt without breaking his tune.

events.text: You swim the mist-shallows alone, with a float of dried gourd and a lung of held breath, and come up between two white ribs of the reef. It is a cathedral of bones, hollow and ringing. Far off, a great slow song starts, and the shelf trembles under your palms.

choices.text: Hold still until the song ends

effects.log: It passes through you like a tide. When it is done, you are not sure that you are the same size.

choices.text: Hurry on before it comes again

effects.log: The song returns twice more, each louder. You are at the far side before the third.

events.text: The safe road follows the shelf's flat top, where the fishers' parties mark the places they will not be left. Rival crews rope themselves together across the thin patches. You tie in with strangers, since there is no other sensible way, and learn their names by dusk.

choices.text: Take the rear of the rope

effects.log: The last place is the worst for slipping and the best for hearing. You return with six stories and a favour owed.

choices.text: Take the lead

effects.log: Whoever goes first tests the shelf, and you do it honestly. The party tells it later as a small saga.

events.text: The beast road drops into the drowned arches where the reef-eels hang like curtains. They are long, pale and curious, and each carries a lantern-bulb on its brow. A hundred bulbs brighten at once, and you see the way ahead through a forest of watching eyes.

choices.text: Hum back at them

effects.log: The curtain shivers and parts. A path of dim bulbs opens, pointing down.

choices.text: Cut through with your hands

effects.log: They slide off you, cold and slick, and the cold stays in your fingers for hours.

events.text: The hidden road is a sunken gallery, and you know the way down by the ache in your teeth. At the bottom, in a niche of reef-bone, is a cloud-pearl wrapped in a net of your own braiding. You gave it back to the reef once, and the reef kept it for you.

choices.text: Take it, and thank the reef

effects.log: The shelf hums, as if pleased. The pearl is cool and weighty and ready.

choices.text: Leave it, and take only a splinter of bone

effects.log: You keep a fragment. The pearl waits for a later, hungrier visit.

events.text: The mother pearl-whale rolls in the mist and looks at you with one huge eye, and then, slowly, rolls away. She was never fighting for the pearls; she was fighting for the calf that sleeps in the lee of the reef. When she sees you will not touch it, she lets you take the one she offers.

choices.text: Take the pearl and keep your distance

effects.log: It is enough. You let the calf sleep.

choices.text: Sing her calf a lullaby

effects.log: It is clumsy and short. The whale hums the end of it for you, a tone you can feel in your sternum.

events.text: The whale lifts out of the mist like a house standing up, and your small boat of bone rocks. She does not strike. She only displaces, in the way of very large things, and you are carried a full mile before the tide sets you down. Her calf is in the far shadow, safe.

choices.text: Paddle home quietly

effects.log: It is a long way, and quiet. You finally feel the mist in your lungs and think it kind.

choices.text: Turn and bow toward her

effects.log: She dips her head, only a little. It is an acknowledgement, not a gift.

events.text: You wade out to the edge of the shelf and lay your palm flat against the mist, as the cloud-fishers do for a fair wind. The whale surfaces under it, huge and quiet, and rests a patch of her skin against your hand. It is cool and damp and softly ridged, and it is a promise.

choices.text: Stay until she sinks

effects.log: It takes an hour. When she is gone your hand keeps the temperature of the deep.

choices.text: Ask for the pearl

effects.log: She exhales a single bead into your palm, as one might lend a coin. It is a loan, and understood as one.

events.text: {sr_sect} welcomes the party home on the dock and sets the cloud-pearl in a bath of sky-water, to be listened to for three nights by the Hall of Tides. The ferrymen sing the verses for the ones who did not come back, and the party stands for each name in silence.

choices.text: Add a name to the song

effects.log: It is the name of someone you met in the reef. The ferryman writes it down and sings it in the next verse.

choices.text: Listen to the pearl with the Hall

effects.log: It sings low and wordless, the whale's lullaby. You cannot say why your eyes sting.

events.text: At the dock a pair of mist-pirates in sea-green sleeves lean on the pilings, faintly bored, as if they have all the time in the world and the tide is theirs. They would like the cloud-pearl. They will take it as a loan, they say, and are lying to a better degree than most.

choices.text: Run the pearl through the fishmarket

effects.log: Among the stalls and baskets you are one more porter. They lose you at the third crossing.

choices.text: Face them with the pearl in hand

effects.log: It sings, loud, a whale-note that rattles every window on the dock. They remember urgent business elsewhere.

events.text: A wet smell has crept through the Sky Archive on the Third Isle, and the oldest scrolls have begun to bead with ink that was not there before. The head archivist whispers that the Drowned Scriptorium is rising: a library that sank with the isle that kept it, still writing in the dark.

choices.text: Ask to read a beaded scroll

effects.log: The ink makes a handwriting you almost recognise. It has written your name, and then crossed it out, and then written it again.

choices.text: Help move the scrolls to dry shelves

effects.log: You haul scrolls until midnight. The archivist presses a very small pastry into your hand, and does not look at you.

variants: The Sky Archive on the Third Isle smells of wet stone, and its oldest scrolls are beading with fresh ink. The head archivist says, very quietly, that the Drowned Scriptorium is rising, still writing in the dark.

events.text: {sr_sect} sends its scribes in as bearers, and you with them. Each carries an oiled-paper satchel and a sealed ink-pot. The leader repeats the rule: read nothing aloud, copy nothing whole. The Scriptorium's doors are open like a mouth mid-sentence. Wet pages sigh on the shelves.

choices.text: Carry the satchel dry

effects.log: The air is damp and mildewed, but your paper stays sound. You walk in like a bridegroom with a gift.

choices.text: Read a title under your breath

effects.log: The shelves shift just slightly, as if someone leaning forward to hear. You do not do that twice.

events.text: You enter through a window of warped glass that no longer closes, into the reading-room where the lamps burn underwater. The desks are slick; the stools swim in place. Every page on every desk is open to a different year, and the ink on all of them is still wet.

choices.text: Read nothing and keep moving

effects.log: It takes will. By the far door you are shaking, with the temptation of a thousand open books at your back.

choices.text: Read one line of a nearby page

effects.log: It is about you. It is accurate, and slightly unkind. You carry it for the rest of the day.

events.text: The safe road follows the cloister-walk, past rows of copyists' cells where inkwells drift. Rival parties pass each other with the stiff courtesy of strangers in a library: nodding, silent, careful with their sleeves. A single cough is a scandal. You walk through like a guest.

choices.text: Nod to every party you pass

effects.log: It is a small courtesy and an honest one. By the last cell, half of them nod back first.

choices.text: Count the cells and their emptiness

effects.log: Thirty-one cells, one with a living ink-trail on the desk. You mark its place.

events.text: The beast road goes through the stacks where silverfish the size of dogs nose among the shelves. They are not hostile, only hungry for paper, and you are carrying a satchel of it. A shiny, whiskered face rises from behind a shelf and sniffs your pocket.

choices.text: Give it a blank sheet

effects.log: It eats the page with a sound like rain. It follows you to the next aisle, hoping for more.

choices.text: Back away and keep the satchel high

effects.log: It stares, and then a dozen more stare. You leave through the narrowest shelf, with a very careful step.

events.text: The hidden road runs behind a shelf of blank-spined books. You press the sixth from the left and the shelf swings. On the far side is a small cell with a desk, an inkpot, and a scroll half-copied in your own hand. The ink is still wet, and the unwritten half is waiting for you to remember it.

choices.text: Finish the line you remember

effects.log: The words come, slowly, in the wrong order, then in the right. The scroll dries gold at the edges.

choices.text: Take the half-scroll as it is

effects.log: Unfinished things are more honest. It rests in your sleeve like an old promise.

events.text: The archivist's ink-shade thins, the black running out of its edges like a spilled quill. It was never a guard, only a last keeper, repeating the oath to guard what was left. When you stand in front of it unflinching, the shade bows and offers the scroll with both hands.

choices.text: Receive the scroll with both hands

effects.log: It weighs as much as a breath. The shade runs back into the shelf, a little ink and no more.

choices.text: Ask the shade what it recorded last

effects.log: It writes in the air: the isle sank at noon. Nobody called the roll. It is a sorrow you did not expect to inherit.

events.text: The shade closes over you like a cuttlefish's cloud. Everything goes black, and cold, and every word you ever said is read to you aloud by a patient voice, in order. It takes an hour. When it is done, the shade withdraws and you are on the cloister floor, hoarse and rather clean.

choices.text: Sit and breathe until you can stand

effects.log: You are still yourself. It is a rare, small victory.

choices.text: Repeat back what it said about you

effects.log: It was accurate. You write it on your wrist so you will not forget the worst of it.

events.text: You walk through the shade by naming nothing and thinking of nothing, an old trick of the silent copyists. It parts like a curtain of wet silk. It does not follow, but you can feel it writing about you, behind, in a fine copperplate that you will never be allowed to read.

choices.text: Hurry on

effects.log: Better a reader than a subject. You leave through a side-door at a trot.

choices.text: Glance back once

effects.log: Your name is written on the air in neat dark ink, then blotted out. A small, strange mercy.

events.text: {sr_sect} spreads the recovered pages on long tables under wet cloths and starts, with infinite patience, to unstick them. The scroll is read by three scribes in turn, each swearing the others to silence. When your turn comes you are shown only the margins. They are full of notes, in a hand like yours.

choices.text: Ask whose hand it is

effects.log: The head scribe pauses, then tells you plainly. It is enough to keep you awake for a week.

choices.text: Copy the margins by memory

effects.log: You are a fast study. By evening you have a clean copy and a stain on your thumb you cannot scrub off.

events.text: On the last stair a rival copyist in cloth-of-silver waits with a wax-sealed warrant and two tall assistants. Their writ says the scroll belongs to the House of Seven Inks. The writ is genuine, and so is the way the assistants are standing: close, and not at ease.

choices.text: Read the writ closely

effects.log: A clerk's error on the fourth line voids it. You point it out gently, and they leave with their dignity folded.

choices.text: Hand over a copy and keep the original

effects.log: You had been making it all through the night. Nobody will ever know which was which.

events.text: Everyone knows there are Eight Houses. Then, once in sixty years, the Archive-keepers go pale and the old ones stop mid-sentence: the Vault of the Ninth House is opening, the House struck from every ledger, and its seal is said to be unbroken still. Nobody agrees why it was struck.

choices.text: Ask an old keeper why the House was struck

effects.log: He looks at the ceiling for a long time and says the ledger forgot, and then that it did not. You leave before he decides which.

choices.text: Look for the Ninth House in the Eight's own records

effects.log: The gaps are tidy. Someone took great care. The tidiness itself is the evidence.

events.text: {sr_sect} files into the Vault behind its banner, but there is a rule above banners: every party is searched at the door by oath-wardens, who ask one question each. Yours is, quite gently, what the party intends to do with a thing that belongs to no one. The leader answers for all, badly.

choices.text: Answer the warden yourself

effects.log: You tell the truth, plainly, and the warden looks relieved. Nobody had answered it so before.

choices.text: Let the leader answer

effects.log: The leader lies, smoothly, and the warden writes it down. It will matter later.

events.text: The Vault has a tradesman's gate for the cartmen who bring the wardens their rice, and a sleepy cartman who was never asked a question in his life. You ride in under a tarp of sacking beside a barrel of pickled ginger. Overhead the Ninth House's great doors stand open, and nobody has ever come back to close them.

choices.text: Stay under the tarp till the doors are behind you

effects.log: The ginger makes your eyes stream. You emerge pale, scented, unseen.

choices.text: Talk to the cartman

effects.log: He has carried rice here for forty years and has never once seen a ward lift a hand. He tells you one name, and begs you not to repeat it.

events.text: The safe road is the Hall of Ledgers: the Ninth House's own rolls, ranged on shelves and read by the rival parties in shifts. A lot of them cry quietly. Whatever the House was, it was loved by someone. You read the Ninth's last entry and carry it through the rest of the Vault.

choices.text: Read it aloud for the others

effects.log: It is a list of the House's servants, with their wages paid in full to the day. A silence follows, a decent one.

choices.text: Read it silently and take notes

effects.log: You write the names, one by one, so that someone will have done it.

events.text: The beast road runs through the Hall of Banners, where the Ninth's crest-beasts are still embroidered on silk that hangs from the rafters. Some of them are not embroidered. A wolf-of-thread climbs down a banner, looks at you with eyes of green silk, and sits to await your courtesy.

choices.text: Bow to the wolf of thread

effects.log: It bows back, exactly as deeply. Then it climbs up and is cloth again.

choices.text: Cut a corner of the banner for proof

effects.log: It tears with a sigh. Every thread-beast in the hall turns its head, and you leave faster than you came.

events.text: You recognise the hidden road by a small notch in the doorframe where you once stood to be measured for a House robe. A past life of yours served the Ninth. The corridor is shorter than your memory says, and at its end is a tiny shrine with a bowl of dust and your old name, written in the House's script.

choices.text: Say the name aloud

effects.log: The shrine glows briefly. The dust becomes a bowl of rice, warm, as if freshly cooked. You eat, because you are asked to.

choices.text: Leave it unsaid and kneel

effects.log: There are names that belong to the dead. You keep the silence, and the shrine seems to approve.

events.text: The oath-wardens lower their halberds, one by one, until only the eldest is left standing. The seal on the dais behind it is unbroken, and it asks, in the old hoarse formal voice: for whom do you take it? You answer truly, and the elder warden bows, slowly, the way a servant bows to a new master and an old friend.

choices.text: Say you take it for the House

effects.log: The wardens exhale as one, a sound like a sail filling. The seal comes off its hook warm.

choices.text: Say you take it for yourself

effects.log: A silence. The elder warden nods, once. Honesty was the only test, and it is passed.

events.text: The wardens do not fight; they hold. Their halberds close in a ring around you and nothing is struck, only withheld. You are held in the middle of the Vault, in the quiet, for as long as it takes you to admit you wanted the seal for the wrong reason. It takes a long time.

choices.text: Admit it

effects.log: The ring opens. It is a small, bitter, clean thing, and you are let go.

choices.text: Wait them out

effects.log: They outlast you. When you finally walk out, it is the slowest exit of your life.

events.text: You slip through the wardens' ring by borrowing a servant's crest from a hook and carrying a tray as if it belonged to you. The wardens' halberds turn to follow, stop, and let you pass, their orders being to question intruders and not servants. The tray holds, absurdly, a pot of cold tea.

choices.text: Set down the tea politely

effects.log: The wardens nod. It is the first time anyone has brought them tea in four hundred years.

choices.text: Keep carrying it as a disguise

effects.log: You make it to the dais with the tea intact and your dignity as well.

events.text: {sr_sect} places the Ninth House's seal in a plain box and sends to all Eight Houses at once, which is the only decent way to tell the truth. The messengers go out in the same hour, so no House can claim to have been told first. The answers will take years. In the meantime the box sits on the table between you, quiet.

choices.text: Stay for the first replies

effects.log: The first House sends back, in one line, the word: finally. You watch your leader read it twice.

choices.text: Leave before the answers

effects.log: Some seals are heavier to watch than to carry. You walk down the hill with lighter shoulders.

events.text: At the last gate a long-sleeved envoy of the Fourth House has been waiting for days, patient and perfumed. The envoy knows the Ninth was struck in the Fourth House's own hand and would like the seal to go quietly into a lacquered box. Behind the envoy, six stewards, none of whom carries a halberd, all of whom stand like they could.

choices.text: Hand it over, with a condition

effects.log: You ask for a written account of the striking. The envoy hesitates, then agrees. The condition will outlive both of you.

choices.text: Walk out by the servants' door

effects.log: It was a gate for the cartmen, once. The stewards cannot enter it without breaking a custom older than all of them.

events.text: Night after night this season the star-river over the Eastern Isles runs a little crooked, as though something at its bed were hammering. The star-watchers keep their charts in tidy rows and refuse to call it a forge. The Star-River Forge, they say, only opens when the river bends. It has bent.

choices.text: Ask a star-watcher about the bend

effects.log: He shows you a chart with a small neat knot in it, and the date, sixty years apart in his own handwriting. He does not say he was there. He does not need to.

choices.text: Watch the river from a rooftop

effects.log: It bends. You are very cold, and very awake, and the sky rings faintly like a struck bowl.

events.text: {sr_sect} anoints each member of the party with a drop of moon-oil on the forehead, to keep the sparks from learning your name. The leader reminds you that a spark remembers. The forge's mouth is a long dark curve under the sky, ringing, and you walk into it in a line of faintly luminous brows.

choices.text: Stand tall under the oil

effects.log: It tingles, then cools. You feel as though you have been stamped as approved.

choices.text: Wipe the oil off

effects.log: The sparks stare. A single one drifts toward you, curious, and lands on your sleeve and sits there, humming.

events.text: The forge has a vent where the starlight cools, a stair of pale slag that hisses underfoot. You climb it in the dark with a rag across your mouth. Above you, the rhythm of the starsmith's hammer falls every ninth heartbeat, and you time your steps to be between.

choices.text: Count to nine and move

effects.log: You settle into the rhythm so fully that you are almost sorry when it stops. You emerge in a hall of light.

choices.text: Move on the hammer-fall

effects.log: Each strike covers your footsteps. It is cleverer and riskier. You get through with a ringing head.

events.text: The safe road is the Tempering Walk, a long gallery lit by half-cooled ingots set into the floor. Rival parties pick their way along it in felt slippers, as one tiptoes through a sleeping house. You pass a party in silver sleeves who nod, briefly, and then pointedly look at your hands.

choices.text: Show your empty hands

effects.log: They relax. It is the oldest courtesy of a forge, and still the best.

choices.text: Nod back and walk on

effects.log: You do not need to prove anything. The silver sleeves watch you out of sight, uneasy.

events.text: The beast road runs through the Quench, a wide cavern where the forge sinks its finished work in pools of cold dark water. Something lives in them: long shapes of dim light, like eels made of the aftermath of stars. They gather at the pool-edge as you pass, mouths open, blinking.

choices.text: Offer them a bright coin of qi

effects.log: They rise, one at a time, to sip. Each one dims a little and brightens you.

choices.text: Walk along the far wall

effects.log: They follow in the water, bewildered, until the Quench narrows. You find you rather miss them.

events.text: The hidden road is a ladder of nine iron rungs behind the great bellows, each rung stamped with a maker's mark that is, unmistakably, yours. You climb in a half-dream. At the top is a small cold forge, no bigger than a hearth, and in it an ingot shaped to your hand.

choices.text: Close your hand on the ingot

effects.log: It is the exact weight of a thing you made and forgot. It warms as you hold it, a small star waking.

choices.text: Put the ingot back and forge a nail instead

effects.log: It is a very small act and a correct one. The little forge hums and approves.

events.text: The starsmith, a constellation that learned to hammer, lowers its hammer. Its shoulders are bright and wide, and its face is no more than a pattern of points. It has made things for ten thousand years and has never once had a customer return them. It holds out its newest ingot, hot, on a tong of light.

choices.text: Take it with a gloved hand

effects.log: It is a falling star, tamed, hot and crooked. It will outlast you.

choices.text: Ask it what it wanted to make

effects.log: A single point of the constellation brightens, then dims. The answer is a name. You hold it in your head like a coal.

events.text: The hammer comes down, not on you but beside you, and the shockwave lays you out on the slag. The starsmith stoops, picks you up in tongs of light, and sets you gently outside the forge door, as one sets down a cat who has wandered into the workshop. Its attention is already back on the anvil.

choices.text: Lie on the slag and laugh

effects.log: The sky rings above you. It is the most gracious defeat you could have asked for.

choices.text: Look at the anvil as you are carried away

effects.log: The ingot it is working has a shape you will remember. You dream of it for months.

events.text: You slip past the starsmith as it bends to the anvil, in the half-heartbeat between strikes, and the hammer comes down on the very spot you stood. Sparks shower. The constellation turns its patterned face toward the place where you were, then turns back. It has seen thieves before. It does not care for most of them.

choices.text: Keep to the shadow of the bellows

effects.log: You edge along the wall to the far door, trailing sparks that sizzle out one by one.

choices.text: Look back and bow

effects.log: It lifts the hammer an inch, a salute. Then the anvil takes all its attention again.

events.text: {sr_sect} puts the falling-star ingot in a vessel of lead and fine silk, and sends it up the long stair of the mountain by relay, runner to runner, each in turn bowing as it passes. Nobody speaks. It is a ritual older than the party and every one of you knows your place in it.

choices.text: Take your turn at the relay

effects.log: Your stretch is the steepest, and the ingot is hot through the silk. You run it up, panting, and hand it on unburnt.

choices.text: Watch from the bottom of the stair

effects.log: You see the whole procession, small bright figures climbing in the dark. It stays with you.

events.text: At the forge's cooling-gate, three grey-sleeved agents of the Brazier Guild wait with a quench-bucket and the unhurried air of tax-collectors. The Guild holds that all star-metal belongs to the Guild. The ingot in your pack is warm. The gate behind you is closing.

choices.text: Hurl the ingot over their heads and run

ok.log: It tumbles end over end, bright as a comet, and you catch it on the far side. The agents shout, and fall behind.

fail.log: The throw falls short and the ingot sizzles into the bucket. You haul it out half-spoiled and pay in blistered fingers.

choices.text: Offer the Guild a sliver for the right of way

effects.log: They weigh the sliver, find it fair, and sign a chit. It is not much and it will save your life someday.

events.text: The tribulation-clouds that failed to break over the Isles in a hundred years have been seen drifting home. The old immortals lock their shutters and tell the children that the Hall of Stored Tribulations is not a place but a debt. It opens every sixty years. It always asks for repayment, in one way or another.

choices.text: Ask what the debt is

effects.log: Every immortal who passed a tribulation left something in the Hall, they say: a fear, a name, a self. The Hall keeps it all.

choices.text: Check your own shutters

effects.log: Nothing there. But you sleep badly, and wake once in the night to a pale flicker at the window.

events.text: {sr_sect} walks its party to the Hall under rain-cloaks, though the sky is clear, and the leader's hands are shaking. At the threshold each member recites the rite of passage for their own tribulation, out loud. You are the last to speak, and it takes you longer than you expected to remember it.

choices.text: Recite it clearly

effects.log: The rite comes back whole, rolling out of you like thunder. The Hall quiets, as if to listen.

choices.text: Recite it quietly

effects.log: You say it under your breath. Somewhere above the doorway a storm-cloud shifts, as if leaning down to hear.

events.text: You find the Hall's drain, a spout through which the clouds spill off the roof when it is full. It is dry, and tall as a house, and its lip is warm to the touch. The air inside smells of burnt copper and rain on a hot street. A hush, and then somewhere far above, a rumble that goes on for an hour.

choices.text: Climb the drain in the lull

effects.log: You time it between rumbles. The grooves worn by a century of water are neat footholds.

choices.text: Wait for the rumble to pass

effects.log: It never quite does. You climb in the thunder's shadow, deaf and grateful.

events.text: The safe road is the Hall of Receipts, where each tribulation is catalogued on a plaque beside its cloud. The rival parties walk the aisles reading aloud, a little too loudly, the names of heroes who failed. One plaque has your own House's crest on it. You read it, and you do not read it aloud.

choices.text: Read it silently and move on

effects.log: It is not a flattering plaque. You carry the facts of it, lightly, in the way of an inheritance.

choices.text: Wipe the dust off the crest

effects.log: Someone is cleaning the plaques, after all. It is you.

events.text: The beast road runs through the Cloud Fold, where the stored storms coil around the stanchions like sleeping dragons. They are not beasts exactly, but they breathe and they turn, and a long lightning-tail drags along the floor behind each one like a cat's. You must pass between them, close enough to smell ozone.

choices.text: Walk calmly and keep your hands out

effects.log: They sense you, rumble once, and let you through. Your hair stands on end for a day.

choices.text: Cross at a run

effects.log: A tail brushes your calf, hot as a stove. You make the far side with a limp and a story.

events.text: The hidden road is a door in a storm that only shows when the lightning is behind you. You step through into a quiet pocket, a small cloud-room with a stool and a lamp. On the stool is a tribulation-seed the size of a plum, with a label in your own writing: Not yet.

choices.text: Take the seed

effects.log: It hums in your hand, impatient and obedient. You feel a little stronger and a great deal more watched.

choices.text: Obey the label and leave it

effects.log: You were wiser once. The seed stays on its stool, and the cloud-room lets you out gently.

events.text: The stored thunderstorm in the judge's face goes quiet, mid-sentence. Its robes uncoil into plain rain, and the lightning in its chest narrows to a candle. It has judged ten thousand claimants, and you are the first to answer without flinching. It hands you the seed, wrapped in a scrap of wet cloud.

choices.text: Receive the seed with thanks

effects.log: It feels like a verdict, not a gift. You carry it as one carries a hard truth.

choices.text: Ask it what it judged

effects.log: Nothing, it says, was ever judged. Only measured. The distinction is a rueful one. You walk away thinking of it.

events.text: The judge-storm hears your plea in full, nods once, and finds you wanting. The sentence is a single bolt, not meant to kill but to remind: it lays you flat on the tiles with your hair smoking, and a smell of burnt sugar in the air. It looks, if anything, sorry.

choices.text: Lie still until the ringing stops

effects.log: You do. It takes a long time, and you learn a great many small things about your own ribs.

choices.text: Ask what the sentence was for

effects.log: It tells you, kindly, in a few precise words. You will think about them for a decade.

events.text: You slip out of the judge's line of sight by passing through a bank of cloud that smells of rain on a particular street. For a moment you are, entirely, a drop of water. The judge-storm looks for you, sees no one, and shuffles its robes. It is a close thing and it knows it.

choices.text: Stay a drop until the gate

effects.log: You hold the stillness for an hour. When you come out the other side, your skin feels a size too large.

choices.text: Leave a small gift of rain

effects.log: A drop of your own breath on a shelf. A courtesy, left for the next supplicant.

events.text: {sr_sect} stores the tribulation-seed in a chest of black iron lined with salt, and sets it in the deepest vault under the main hall, with three locks and three keepers. The keepers each swear the oath, and each is told what the seed is for. Each of them, afterward, looks a little older.

choices.text: Ask to be one of the keepers

effects.log: You are asked to wait. It is a long wait. They come back, in the end, with a key for you.

choices.text: Decline politely

effects.log: Some responsibilities find you regardless. This one will not, and you are glad.

events.text: On the stair down, a thin angry man in the black sleeves of the Storm-Watch steps out of a doorway and says that the seed belongs to the Watch. He has a warrant, and also a pair of weighted rods that glow faintly at the tips. It is not clear which of those he intends to rely on. He is breathing hard from the run.

choices.text: Argue the law with him

effects.log: You do it slowly, and kindly, until he forgets which rod is which. The warrant's date, you note, is wrong.

choices.text: Lead him round the long stair

effects.log: He follows, sweating, trailing sparks. By the bottom you have lost him in a crowd of pilgrims.

events.text: A great shadow has crossed the Western Isles in broad daylight, slow as a thought, and the ferrymen have all stopped work to watch it. Under it the mist is warm. The Sky-Whale, asleep for nine hundred years, is turning in its dream, and the old charts say that its mouth opens once in sixty years to let the lost find home.

choices.text: Climb to the cliffs to watch it pass

effects.log: It takes an hour, and you lose the sun twice under its shadow. It is the largest thing you have ever seen, and you are not afraid.

choices.text: Ask the ferrymen what the whale swallowed

effects.log: Whole cloud-ships, they say, and the islands they sailed from. Some of them are still inside, and singing.

events.text: {sr_sect} boards the party onto a flat cloud-barge, and the leader says nothing, because nothing needs to be said. The whale's mouth is a cavern with a tide in it. The barge rides the swell inward on a warm wind, past teeth the size of towers, into the green dark. Every one of you holds your breath.

choices.text: Breathe out slowly and trust the wind

effects.log: It is warm and smells of ocean. The barge carries you on, like a rocked child.

choices.text: Count the teeth as you pass

effects.log: There are ninety-one. You have the number by heart, and the barge has a small pleasant surprise for the thirty-third.

events.text: You wait on a drifting spar until the great mouth gapes, and then leap, with a rope tied to a cloud-gull's leg, onto the tongue. It is warm, and wide as a plaza, and slightly ridged. The air in the whale smells of salt, old wood and pickled fruit. Far ahead, a pale light pulses with a slow heartbeat.

choices.text: Follow the pulse of light

effects.log: It beats once every twelve breaths. By matching your stride you save yourself an hour.

choices.text: Scramble up the palate

effects.log: The ridges make steps. You climb in a cool damp dark and come out above the lantern-lit gullet.

events.text: The safe road follows the Gullet, a wide ribbed tunnel hung with drifting wreckage that the whale swallowed and has never forgotten: spars, masts, cloud-ship figureheads staring at nothing. Rival parties pick over the wreckage politely, sorting salvage into piles by flag. You keep to the middle, where the footing is firmest.

choices.text: Help a party free a stuck figurehead

effects.log: It comes out with a groan. Its wooden face has a nose you almost know. You say nothing, and help to carry it.

choices.text: Read the flags on the wreckage

effects.log: Thirty-one Houses, none of them still extant. You catalogue them as an honest historian would.

events.text: The beast road runs through the Gill Gardens, a damp warm bank of pale fronds that filter the whale's breath. Small bright creatures live among them: fish with legs, crabs with wings. They cling to your sleeves like burrs and refuse to be shaken, chirping in an unknown tongue that sounds suspiciously like gossip.

choices.text: Let them ride along

effects.log: They settle on your shoulders like a mantle of sequins. Several of them drop off at the next bend with a wave.

choices.text: Brush them away gently

effects.log: They go, offended. A frond slaps your face, almost fondly.

events.text: The hidden road is the whale's old swallowing-groove, hardly more than a crack in the ribs. You remember it as you would a lullaby you hated. At its end is a hollow in the ribs where a small child's cot once rested, and on the cot a pearl, yours, left to be found by whoever would come back.

choices.text: Take the pearl

effects.log: It is cool, round and old. The whale hums faintly around you in recognition.

choices.text: Lie down on the cot a moment

effects.log: It is the shortest nap of your life and the best. You wake with nothing missing and something added.

events.text: The great whale opens one eye, a pool of dim gold the size of a lake. It has not been awake for nine hundred years, and its first thought is not anger but a vast sleepy surprise. It looks at you for a long moment and lets go of the pearl it has held in its throat since the first wreck.

choices.text: Bow, and take the pearl with both hands

effects.log: It is warm and humming, a thing the whale has hummed to itself for centuries. It fits your palm as if made for it.

choices.text: Ask the whale to sleep again

effects.log: It closes its eye. The belly settles. Nothing is taken; something is given, and you feel the weight of it.

events.text: The whale does not wake. It dreams, and in the dream you are a speck, and the dream sneezes. You are borne out of the Gullet on a tide of warm brine, tumbled in a ring of wreckage, and set down on the barge like a coin spat out. The whale sighs, and the cavern settles into a long rest.

choices.text: Wave at the mouth as it closes

effects.log: The whale's great eye is shut. But you wave anyway. It seems the thing to do.

choices.text: Count your bruises

effects.log: Eleven, and one good story. The whale remains unbothered.

events.text: You lay your palm on the warm ridged wall of the Gullet and hum the lullaby the ferrymen use for the shadow. The whale hears it through the whole length of its body. It does not wake, but its slow heartbeat adjusts to your hum, and the pearl comes loose into your hand, drawn by a tide of kindness.

choices.text: Keep humming until the pulse steadies

effects.log: It takes an hour. At the end your throat is raw and your heart feels three sizes too big.

choices.text: Thank it in the old ferry-song

effects.log: The whale rumbles. In your chest, a tiny pearl-sized answer.

events.text: {sr_sect} hangs the whale's pearl in the Hall of Tides, in a cradle of sky-silk, and sends boats out to meet the whale on its way. The ferrymen sing it north. The shadow moves over the water like a blessing, and you are told the Hall will keep the pearl only until the whale wakes and wants it back.

choices.text: Join the ferrymen in the song

effects.log: Your voice is not good, but it is willing. The shadow passes over you, warm and enormous.

choices.text: Stay by the pearl overnight

effects.log: It hums softly. You sleep better than you have in years, and wake to find your lamp has been trimmed by a stranger.

events.text: At the Mouth, a crooked pair of wreckers stand with a boat-hook and a net, whistling, waiting for what the whale spits out. They are not wicked. They are hungry, and the pearl looks like dinner. The younger of them keeps looking at the ground. The elder is looking at your pack.

choices.text: Give them a share of the wreckage you carry

effects.log: Salvage is salvage. They take a coil of rope and a figurehead, and let you pass with the pearl.

choices.text: Go round by the tongue-ridge

effects.log: They watch you go, nets drooping. You hear them arguing about it all the way down the shore.

events.text: The Hollow Peak has begun to answer. On still nights the villagers of the high terraces hear voices from its summit, voices of the dead, repeating a question that is clearly meant for someone else. The Peak of Echoes opens once in sixty years, and the Archive says: it keeps the answer to whatever you ask it, if you can climb that far.

choices.text: Listen from the terrace by night

effects.log: The question comes down on the wind: and what will you do then? It sounds like your own voice, and a little like someone who loved you.

choices.text: Write down your question beforehand

effects.log: It takes three attempts. The last is the shortest. You fold it small and keep it in your sleeve.

events.text: {sr_sect} ascends in file by the Pilgrim's Stair, a road of seven thousand steps cut into the Peak's flank, each marked with a name. The leader tells you to say each name softly as you tread on it. A great many are the names of the dead, and the stair seems pleased that anyone remembered.

choices.text: Say every name you can read

effects.log: By the three-thousandth step your voice is gone. You mouth the rest, and the stair does not mind.

choices.text: Count the steps and skip the names

effects.log: You reach the summit first by half an hour. Nobody thanks you, and nobody blames you, either.

events.text: You go up the north face by the goat-track, in the lee of the wind, where nobody ever climbs because it is steep and because it echoes. Your own footfall comes back a breath late, then a breath earlier. Somewhere below, a stone dislodges, and you hear it fall three times.

choices.text: Climb quietly, to deny the echoes a voice

effects.log: It is a skill like holding a cup full to the brim. You arrive at the first ledge dry-mouthed and unobserved.

choices.text: Call out and let the echo tell you the height

effects.log: It answers in forty heartbeats. You are further up than you feared, and nearer than you hoped.

events.text: The safe road runs along the Whispering Terrace, a ledge hung with prayer-flags that repeat to the wind every word spoken near them. Rival parties talk quietly of trivial things, to avoid giving the flags anything to repeat. The flags, bored, repeat the quiet. It is a strange, monastic, faintly comic procession.

choices.text: Say something cheerful to the flags

effects.log: They repeat it, cheerfully. A whole terrace murmurs: lovely weather, lovely weather. The parties laugh despite themselves.

choices.text: Walk in silence and listen

effects.log: The flags are repeating what was said yesterday, and the day before. You catch the end of a conversation of long ago.

events.text: The beast road runs through the Goat Halls, a broken terrace where the Peak's mountain-goats graze among echoes. They are quick, shaggy and watchful, and their bleat comes back to you in the voices of people you knew. A big grey nanny steps onto the path, looks you in the eye, and says, in a voice you almost know: not that way.

choices.text: Take the other way

effects.log: It was a good tip. The path she meant has a hidden drop. You thank her, belatedly, with a handful of salt.

choices.text: Go the way she warned against

effects.log: She stamps, and a chorus of bleats rings out around you. You pick your way down through them, scraped but alive.

events.text: The hidden road is a cleft you recognise by the way your breath catches. You climbed it, once, in a life when you did not return. Halfway up the cleft is a niche with a lamp in it, still burning, and by the lamp a rolled note. It says: ask the question you wrote down, and no other.

choices.text: Ask the question you wrote down

effects.log: The cleft takes the question and goes quiet for a long time. The answer comes up from the dark, three words, unmistakable.

choices.text: Ask a different question

effects.log: The cleft goes very quiet. After a while it answers anyway, and you are not sure it was kind.

events.text: The echo of every failed climber rises around you, a ring of pale outlines, and each one in turn bows to you. They are not enemies; they are the Peak's memory of what it is to want a thing and not reach it. When the last has bowed, the summit-stone gives up its answer, a single note that lingers in your chest.

choices.text: Hold the note until it fades

effects.log: It lasts a long time. By the end of it you know a little more than you did.

choices.text: Bow to the climbers in return

effects.log: Each one smiles, or something like a smile. They do not speak, but they remain with you in a way that is not unkind.

events.text: The echoes crowd in, all your own voice at different ages, saying all the things you did not say. They do not strike. They only speak, softly, closer and closer, until you sink onto the stone and put your hands over your ears. It does not help. They stop only when you stop wanting them to.

choices.text: Listen to the last one

effects.log: It is the youngest voice, and it says only: it is all right. You are carried down in tears and mostly in peace.

choices.text: Shout back at them

effects.log: The Peak shouts back, in thirty voices, and you are very tired afterward. You have been heard, and that was something.

events.text: You slip past the echoes by not answering. Each one leans toward you, expecting a reply, and goes on waiting while you pass. It is the hardest silence you have ever kept. At the summit you are aware of a great chorus at your back, still waiting politely for you to say something.

choices.text: Say nothing, all the way down

effects.log: It takes the best part of a day. You come out with a stiff jaw and a very clear head.

choices.text: Leave one word on the summit for them

effects.log: You say it, once. The Peak takes it and rings it back, softly, over and over, until the last climber is out of earshot.

events.text: {sr_sect} carries the answer home as a sealed question, since the Peak's reply may not be said aloud on the Isles. The elders gather in a closed room. When the door opens each of them looks a little older and a little lighter. Nobody will tell you what was said, but your name is mentioned, kindly, at supper.

choices.text: Ask nothing

effects.log: Some answers are better left sealed. The elder who sees you decline gives a slow, grave nod.

choices.text: Ask what they learned about you

effects.log: They tell you a little, carefully. It is neither flattering nor cruel, only exact.

events.text: At the foot of the Stair, hooded pilgrims in the gold of the Seeker Lodge stop you with polite hands. They have climbed for years to ask the Peak a question and found it closed, and they ask, with real humility, what you were told. Behind them, six more pilgrims, not hooded, with staves. They are not here to ask.

choices.text: Tell them what the Peak said, and nothing else

effects.log: The hooded ones weep. The ones with staves look at each other and lower them. It was the one thing that could stop it.

choices.text: Duck into the crowd of descending pilgrims

effects.log: There are hundreds. They cannot tell one weary face from another. You are three terraces away before they notice.

events.text: A scent of green and bitter smoke is blowing through the Pill Quarter, unlike anything in a living garden. The old apothecaries pull the shutters on their shop-fronts and mutter. The Garden of the First Alchemist opens once in sixty years: the place where the elixir was first grown, and the place where it was first lost.

choices.text: Ask an apothecary what was lost

effects.log: The first elixir, she says, but also the first alchemist. Perhaps they were the same thing. She sniffs the wind once more and goes in.

choices.text: Follow the scent to the Quarter's edge

effects.log: It leads to an old drainpipe, green with moss. A single white flower grows there, impossibly, and nods at you.

events.text: {sr_sect} brings its own physician to walk at the party's back with a satchel of antidotes, because the Garden poisons the careless. The leader reads the rules aloud: touch nothing, eat nothing, bow at every gate. The first gate is a trellis of living thorn, and it parts only for those who bow without being told.

choices.text: Bow at the thorns before anyone tells you

effects.log: They draw aside with a rustle like a satisfied sigh. The physician makes a note.

choices.text: Wait to be told

effects.log: The thorns wait with you. The leader bows, then the rest. You bow last, and a thorn catches your sleeve in passing.

events.text: You enter over the compost wall, where the first alchemist's failed batches were buried. The ground is warm and slightly alive. Things sprout from it: little green faces on stalks, which open their mouths as you cross. You step lightly, as you would on a sleeping person's hand.

choices.text: Step only on bare earth

effects.log: There is not much of it. You pick your way across by hops and balance, and the faces track you, hopeful.

choices.text: Cover your nose and run

effects.log: The spores catch you anyway. For an hour the world is slightly more cheerful than it should be.

events.text: The safe road is the Herb-Walk, a straight gravelled path between beds of labelled plants, the first catalogue in the world. Rival parties walk it reading the labels, and arguing, in tight polite voices, over which labels are lies. You find a plant tagged with your own House's name and a note: poisonous in the wrong hands.

choices.text: Read the full note

effects.log: The right hands are described, in detail. They are not yours, but they might become so.

choices.text: Join the argument on the labels

effects.log: You settle three disputes by smell. A rival apothecary tips her hat to you, and means it.

events.text: The beast road passes the Bee Colonnade, a hall of hives as big as houses, and the bees who tend them, each the size of a hand and gilded like a coin. They do not sting the humble, an old rule runs, only the proud. You find, to your discomfort, that you have no idea which you are.

choices.text: Walk through with your hands open

effects.log: They hum around you in a golden cloud. One lands on your wrist and sits, warm, then lifts off again.

choices.text: Walk fast with your head down

effects.log: Only one stings. It is a small, pointed, specific sting, and you deserve it.

events.text: The hidden road is a ladder inside the trunk of a hollow tree you planted, once, with your own hands. The ladder is made of your own handholds worn into the wood. At the top is a small greenhouse, glass fogged with age, and in it a seedling that has waited a lifetime for you to come back and finish watering it.

choices.text: Water the seedling

effects.log: It unfurls, a single leaf at a time, and you feel the life of it, quiet and enormous.

choices.text: Take a cutting and leave it growing

effects.log: The seedling does not mind. You carry the cutting in damp cloth like a letter you will answer later.

events.text: The gardener, who is also the first harvest, a figure of vine and root with a face like a pressed flower, stops with its shears in the air. It has pruned the Garden for ten thousand years, and it sees in you someone who knows when a branch should be cut and when it should be left. It sets the shears down and offers a seed in its green palm.

choices.text: Accept the seed

effects.log: It is small and warm and full of intent. The gardener closes its hand around yours for a moment, then lets go.

choices.text: Ask what it would grow, if it could choose

effects.log: It tells you. It is a very small, specific tree, and you will plant one when you can.

events.text: The gardener prunes you. It does not use the shears for harm; it merely finds the places where you are overgrown, and trims. A confidence, a false certainty, a sharpness of temper. You are left lighter by several things, in a bed of fresh clippings, and a little bewildered at how little it hurt.

choices.text: Gather the clippings and thank it

effects.log: It cocks its head. A gardener has not been thanked in a long time. It hands you a handkerchief of moss.

choices.text: Refuse to be tidied

effects.log: The gardener shrugs, and leaves you in the mulch. You grow your own way, awkwardly, for a while.

events.text: You slip past the gardener by standing very still among the hedge-statues, one among many, hands raised in a pose of reverent confusion. It trims you twice, just in case, and moves on, whistling dryly through its leaves. You step down with a haircut you did not ask for.

choices.text: Keep the haircut

effects.log: It is a very good haircut, in fact. You are told so twice before the gate.

choices.text: Trim the statue next to you in return

effects.log: It is a courtesy, of a sort. The gardener, passing, nods approval at the neatness.

events.text: {sr_sect} plants the seed of the first elixir in the Garden of the Sect itself, under glass, and sets a rota of watchers. The leader reads out the names: one for each season. Yours is autumn, the season of harvest and of letting go. The seed, in its black soil, is already stirring.

choices.text: Accept the autumn watch

effects.log: It is a long vigil and a quiet one. In the end, the seedling lets you see it grow.

choices.text: Ask for spring instead

effects.log: The rota is shuffled. Spring is asked for more often than autumn, and you are given a strange look.

events.text: At the Garden's last gate an apothecary in the indigo of the Pharmacopoeia Guild is waiting, with a basket of lilies and a ledger of claims. The Guild holds that all first-elixir seeds are Guild property, and that the Guild always pays. The lilies smell sweet, too sweet, and the basket is heavy at the bottom.

choices.text: Refuse the lilies and the ledger

effects.log: You step round the basket politely. The apothecary's smile does not move, but the basket does, slightly.

choices.text: Trade a cutting for safe passage

effects.log: The Guild accepts a lesser seed. You pocket the greater one, and walk on, lightly poorer in honesty and richer in everything else.

events.text: The parties gather on the cloud-quay of {sr_realm}, banners lifting in the thin wind, and names are called from a lacquered list. {sr_sect} has chosen its entrants. Yours is not among them. You watch the chosen walk into the mist, and the barrier folds shut behind them like a page.

choices.text: Look along the barrier for a seam

effects.log: Barriers are woven, and weaving has ends. You walk its edge like a tailor, noting where the thread runs thin.

choices.text: Go back to the practice terrace

effects.log: Next time they will call your name. You decide it, there on the quay, quite calmly.

choices.text: Swallow it

effects.log: It goes down hard and stays down. You breathe the thin air until it settles.

events.text: No party takes you in. You stand at the edge of the quay beneath the Isle-lanterns while the Houses' colours file past toward {sr_realm}, and nobody so much as looks at you. A tea-seller, packing up her stall, asks if you are lost. You laugh a little, and say no.

choices.text: Buy her last cup and sit on the quay

effects.log: It is the best tea of the year, bitter and plain. She tells you a story about her sister in the mist, and you listen to all of it.

choices.text: Walk the barrier alone

effects.log: There is a thin place north of the quay where the mist is only a veil. You mark it for later.

events.text: A great realm is opening and the lists are stern. Only the best of every banner are called, and the rest stand about in good clothes. You hear a young disciple behind you whisper that the choosing was fair. You know that it was, which is the worst part. The mist rises, and the chosen go in.

choices.text: Wish the chosen well aloud

effects.log: Several turn to nod. It costs nothing, and it lands somewhere.

choices.text: Memorise who was chosen and why

effects.log: A list is a map of what a banner values. You study it on the long walk home.

choices.text: Turn your back on the barrier

effects.log: It is easier. It is not wise, but it is easier, and you walk home lighter.

events.text: {npc} walks beside you through {sr_realm}, close enough that your sleeves brush in the narrow places. Neither of you says much. At a fork {he} stops and looks at you, and you realise {he} has been waiting all day for you to choose the way, because {he} trusts you to.

choices.text: Choose, and choose well

mem.note: chose the road for us in the sealed realm, and chose well

effects.log: You pick the left. It is the right way. {npc} lets out a breath {he} did not know {he} was holding.

choices.text: Ask {him} to choose

mem.note: asked me to choose the road in the sealed realm

effects.log: {He} picks the right, surprised to be asked. It is the longer way, and the prettier one.

events.text: You and {npc} grew up fighting over everything, and inside {sr_realm} you fight over the map, the water-gourd, and which of you is in charge. Then something sighs in the dark ahead and {he} catches your sleeve, the way {he} did when you were both small. Neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Take {his} hand

mem.note: held my hand in the dark of the sealed realm

effects.log: You hold on until the sighing stops. Then you both let go at once and argue about the map again.

choices.text: Tease {him} about it later

mem.note: teased me about the dark of the sealed realm

effects.log: At the next fire you bring it up. {He} throws a pinecone at you. It is the most ordinary thing that has happened all day.

events.text: {npc} reaches for your hand at the crossing of {sr_realm}, where the mist is thick enough to lose a person in. It is a plain gesture, practised over many years. You hold on tightly as the world dims, and for a long moment there is only the warmth of one palm and the smell of {his} hair-oil.

choices.text: Hold on until the mist thins

mem.note: held on through the mist of the sealed realm

effects.log: It takes an hour. You come out the other side with {npc}'s hand still in yours, and neither of you remarks on it.

choices.text: Tie a cord between you

mem.note: tied us together in the mist of the sealed realm

effects.log: It is practical and kind. You walk on, linked, and the mist can do nothing about it.

events.text: {npc} follows two paces behind you through {sr_realm}, as a good disciple does, carrying more than {he} should and complaining of nothing. At the first camp {he} lays out your bedroll before {his} own. {He} is watching your face for the verdict on the day, without wanting to be seen watching.

choices.text: Tell {him} plainly what {he} did well

mem.note: told me what I did well in the sealed realm

effects.log: {He} flushes to the ears and says nothing. But next day {he} walks a little taller, and carries a little less.

choices.text: Make {him} sit and eat before you do

mem.note: made me eat first in the sealed realm

effects.log: {He} protests. You insist. It is a small thing, and it is the thing {he} will remember.
